# Adding HTML

#### Course: Learn CSS

## Adding HTML

Let's start by writing the basic HTML structure for the contact form. This will include input fields such as text, email, dropdowns, and a submit button.

Additionally, we'll add a browser reset to remove any default styling and provide a clean foundation for custom CSS.

```html
1<form class="contact-form">
2    <h2>Contact Us</h2>
3
4    <div class="form-group">
5        <label for="fullname">Full Name</label>
6        <input type="text" id="fullname" name="fullname" placeholder="Your Full Name" required>
7    </div>
8
9    <div class="form-group">
10        <label for="email">Email Address</label>
11        <input type="email" id="email" name="email" placeholder="your@email.com" required>
12    </div>
13
14    <div class="form-group">
15        <label for="subject">Subject</label>
16        <input type="text" id="subject" name="subject" placeholder="Subject of your message" required>
17    </div>
18
19    <div class="form-group">
20        <label for="reason">Reason for Contact</label>
21        <select id="reason" name="reason" required>
22            <option value="" disabled selected>Select a reason</option>
23            <option value="networking">Networking</option>
24            <option value="freelance">Freelance</option>
25            <option value="support">Support</option>
26            <option value="feedback">Feedback</option>
27            <option value="other">Other</option>
28        </select>
29    </div>
30
31    <div class="form-group">
32        <label for="message">Message</label>
33        <textarea id="message" name="message" placeholder="Your message..." rows="5" required></textarea>
34    </div>
35
36    <button type="submit" class="submit-btn">Send Message</button>
37</form>
```

```css
1/* Basic reset */
2* {
3    margin: 0;
4    padding: 0;
5    box-sizing: border-box;
6}
```
